investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the agent pod because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable units remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node, the pod remained Pending for ~142–147 seconds until the eval timed out. No VM was provisioned, so vmIdPresent and remoteState were never written, and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259) could not be satisfied. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration problem localized to the remote-agent swarm cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler message, pod stuck for 147s, no evidence keys collected.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150391, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the eval ran to completion and was not itself truncated.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — this is the call that triggers pod scheduling; failure here prevents all downstream evidence writes.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no free VM slots remain for a new agent pod, and preemption found no evictable victims.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, leaving 4 general-purpose nodes ineligible regardless of their available capacity.
[Possible] A prior eval run or a leaked agent pod is holding the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on one or both eligible nodes, preventing new allocations.
[Possible] The cluster was scaled down or a kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node was cordoned/drained around the time of the eval run (2026-07-04T21:14–21:21Z), reducing available capacity to zero.

[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than any single node can provide) could make the pod permanently unschedulable even when nodes have partial capacity.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking All Remote Agent Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the state-polling phase, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, 2 that carry the kata peer-pods VM resource have none remaining, and the other 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 resource-bearing nodes and preemption is not applicable to the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. This caused every remote-agent pod creation attempt to remain Unschedulable for ~142–147 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing any agent lifecycle progress and leaving all required evidence fields empty.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots consumed, leaving none available for the eval probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates for remote-agent pods. If those 2 nodes have a small VM quota, any concurrent usage will exhaust capacity.

Tertiary — VM slot leak: a previous eval run's cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs:1903) may have failed to release kata peer-pod VM slots, leaving the resource counter depleted for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any production remote-agent workloads running at the same time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the agent pod because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable units remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node, the pod remained Pending for ~142–147 seconds until the eval timed out. No VM was provisioned, so vmIdPresent and remoteState were never written, and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259) could not be satisfied. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration problem localized to the remote-agent swarm cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 142s, no evidence keys collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler message, pod stuck for 147s, no evidence keys collected.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the pod never starting.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150391, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the eval ran to completion and was not itself truncated.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — this is the call that triggers pod scheduling; failure here prevents all downstream evidence writes.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no free VM slots remain for a new agent pod, and preemption found no evictable victims.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, leaving 4 general-purpose nodes ineligible regardless of their available capacity.
[Possible] A prior eval run or a leaked agent pod is holding the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on one or both eligible nodes, preventing new allocations.
[Possible] The cluster was scaled down or a kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node was cordoned/drained around the time of the eval run (2026-07-04T21:14–21:21Z), reducing available capacity to zero.

[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than any single node can provide) could make the pod permanently unschedulable even when nodes have partial capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking All Remote Agent Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the state-polling phase, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, 2 that carry the kata peer-pods VM resource have none remaining, and the other 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 resource-bearing nodes and preemption is not applicable to the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. This caused every remote-agent pod creation attempt to remain Unschedulable for ~142–147 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing any agent lifecycle progress and leaving all required evidence fields empty.
